correctness.rationale: Projector formulas follow from the strongly regular quadratic adjacency identity; the positive and zero kernel types are calculated for all vertex pairs. Nonedge sign is controlled exactly by a one-hump two-exponential scalar function; its unique return zero is proved, not sampled. The positive recovery root depends smoothly on the coupling, vanishes at both endpoints, and its stationary condition forces a strictly monotone spectral ratio, proving one and only one global maximizer with the stated explicit formulas. 392 direct matrix exponential checks independently reproduce the finite examples, without being used as an infinite proof.

The full-coupling multipartite theorem is a proper graph-class special case (only regular multipartite graphs are strongly regular), whereas the new result also covers pentagon, Petersen, triangular and Paley graphs. General eventual-positivity theory supplies no sharp finite cutoff, and Padé steps use distinct spectral functions.

value.rationale: This gives a complete time-domain positivity classification and a closed-form globally worst mixing-strength law for the natural, extensive three-Laplacian-eigenvalue graph class. The critical parameter of mixed second- and fourth-order diffusion is motivated by the extent of transient negative kernels, and primitive examples beyond the earlier regular multipartite cases show the result is structurally new rather than a restated special case.
